newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia and China sign document on new world order.
newsitem.headline: Russia and China sign document on new world order.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin and Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Wednesday signed a political declaration which the Russian leader called an unprecedented document aimed at preventing world domination by any country.
"We have not signed such a document with any other country," Yeltsin, 66, who looked stiff but composed, said in televised remarks after a signing ceremony.
The text of the declaration was not made public.

"Someone is longing for a single-polar world. He wants to decide things himself," Yeltsin, standing next to the smiling Jiang, 70, said. "But we want the world to be multi-polar. Those poles will form the basis of the new international order."

Yeltsin did not mention any country but his remark appeared to refer to claims by the United States for the leading role in the post-Cold War world which have aroused opposition both in Moscow and Beijing.
Russia, deeply alarmed by NATO's plans to expand eastwards, is looking for new allies which could diversify its foreign policy, focused mainly on the West after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
But Russian officials said Moscow did not view rapprochement with Beijing as a means to counter-balance NATO's plans to grant membership to some Eastern European countries.
"The very suggestion of plans to create some counter-blocs are wrong and counter-productive," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.
Yeltsin said he and Jiang also managed to solve a number of problems which were obstacles to developing bilateral ties.
"We have discussed more than 20 issues with the Chinese partners including border problems, the number of forces deployed along our common border and nuclear energy," he said.
Russia, China, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan are due to sign on Thursday a treaty on troop reductions along the former Soviet-Chinese border.
